verses.1:1: In the eighth month, in the second year of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:
verses.1:2: "The Lord was angry against your fathers with wrath.
verses.1:3: And you will say to them, 'This is what the Lord of hosts says: Turn back to Me, declares the Lord of hosts, and I will turn back to you, says the Lord of hosts.
verses.1:4: Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets cried out, saying, "This is what the Lord of hosts says: Turn back from your evil ways and from your most wicked thoughts." And they did not listen, nor did they pay attention to Me, says the Lord.
verses.1:5: Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, will they live forever?
verses.1:6: Yet My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, did they not overtake your fathers? And they turned back and said, "Just as the Lord of hosts intended to do to us according to our ways and according to our devices, He has done to us."'"
verses.1:7: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:
verses.1:8: I saw during the night, and look, a man riding on a red horse; and he himself was standing among the myrtle groves that were in the depth, and behind him were red, dappled, and white horses.
verses.1:9: And I said, "What are these, my lord?" And the angel who was speaking in me said to me, "I will show you what these are."
verses.1:10: And the man who was standing among the myrtle groves answered and said, "These are the ones whom the Lord has sent to walk throughout the earth."
verses.1:11: And they answered the angel of the Lord, who was standing among the myrtle groves, and said, "We have walked throughout the earth, and look, all the earth is inhabited and is at rest."
verses.1:12: And the angel of the Lord answered and said, "Lord of hosts, how long will You not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, with which You have been angry? This is now the seventieth year."
verses.1:13: And the Lord answered the angel who was speaking in me with good words, comforting words.
verses.1:14: And the angel who was speaking in me said to me, "Cry out, saying, 'This is what the Lord of hosts says: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with great jealousy,
verses.1:15: and with great anger I am angry against the wealthy nations, because I was a little angry, yet they themselves helped toward evil.
verses.1:16: Therefore this is what the Lord says: I will return to Jerusalem with mercies, and My house will be built in it, declares the Lord of hosts, and a plumb line will be stretched over Jerusalem.'
verses.1:17: Cry out again, saying, 'This is what the Lord of hosts says: My cities will again overflow with good things, and the Lord will again comfort Zion and will again choose Jerusalem.'"
verses.2:1: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, four horns.
verses.2:2: And I said to the angel who was speaking in me, "What are these?" And he said to me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
verses.2:3: And the Lord showed me four craftsmen.
verses.2:4: And I said, "What are these coming to do?" And he spoke, saying, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, man by man, and none of them lifted up his head; and these have come to terrify them, so that they may cast down the horns of the nations that lifted up a horn over the land of Judah to disperse it."
verses.2:5: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a man, and in his hand was a measurers' cord.
verses.2:6: And I said, "Where are you going?" And he said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, and to see how great its width is and how great its length is."
verses.2:7: And look, the angel who was speaking in me was going out, and another angel was going out to meet him;
verses.2:8: and he said to him, "Run, speak to that young man, saying, 'Jerusalem will be inhabited without a wall, because of the multitude of people and livestock in its midst.
verses.2:9: And I will be to it, declares the Lord, a wall of fire all around, and I will be in glory in its midst.'"
verses.2:10: "Oh! Oh! Flee from the land of the north," says the Lord, "for I have dispersed you into the four winds of heaven," says the Lord.
verses.2:11: Oh, Zion! Flee, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon,
verses.2:12: for this is what the Lord of hosts says: "After glory He has sent Me to the nations that plundered you; for whoever touches you touches the pupil of My eye.
verses.2:13: For look, I raise My hand over them, and they will become plunder for those who were serving them; and you will know that the Lord of hosts has sent Me.
verses.2:14: Give praise and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for look, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst," declares the Lord.
verses.2:15: "And many nations will be joined to the Lord in that day, and they will be a people to Me, and I will dwell in your midst; and you will know that the Lord of hosts has sent Me to you."
verses.2:16: And the Lord will possess Judah as His portion in the sanctified land, and He will again choose Jerusalem.
verses.2:17: Let all flesh be silent before the face of the Lord, for He has risen up from His holy dwelling.
verses.3:1: And the Lord showed me Joshua the high priest, standing before the angel of the Lord; and Satan was standing at his right hand to oppose him.
verses.3:2: And the Lord said to Satan, "May the Lord rebuke you, Satan! And may the Lord who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Is this one not a burning stick snatched from the fire?"
verses.3:3: And Joshua was clothed in filthy garments, and he was standing before the face of the angel.
verses.3:4: He answered and spoke to those who were standing before him, saying, "Remove the filthy garments from him." And he said to him, "Look, I have removed your iniquity from you, and I have clothed you with fresh garments."
verses.3:5: And he said, "Place a clean turban on his head." And they placed a clean turban on his head and clothed him with garments; and the angel of the Lord was standing by.
verses.3:6: And the angel of the Lord solemnly charged Joshua, saying,
verses.3:7: "This is what the Lord of hosts says: If you walk in My ways and keep My charge, you also will judge My house and will keep My courts, and I will give you those who walk from among these who now stand here.
verses.3:8: Listen, Joshua the high priest, you and your friends who dwell before you, for they are foreshadowing men: for look, I will bring My servant, the Dawn.
verses.3:9: For look, the stone that I have placed before Joshua: on one stone are seven eyes; look, I will carve its engraving, declares the Lord of hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.
verses.3:10: In that day, says the Lord of hosts, each man will invite his friend under the vine and under the fig tree."
verses.4:1: And the angel who was speaking in me returned, and roused me like a man who is roused from his sleep.
verses.4:2: And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I have seen, and look, a lampstand entirely of gold, and its lamp on top of it, and its seven oil lamps on it, and seven funnels for the oil lamps that were on top of it,
verses.4:3: and two olive trees above it, one on the right of the lamp, and one on its left."
verses.4:4: And I answered and said to the angel who was speaking in me, saying, "What are these, my lord?"
verses.4:5: And the angel who was speaking in me answered and said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
verses.4:6: And he answered and said to me, saying, "This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel, saying, 'Not by an army, nor by strength, but by My Spirit,' says the Lord of hosts.
verses.4:7: 'Who are you, great mountain, before Zerubbabel? Into a plain! And he will bring out the primary stone, and he will make grace equal to its grace.'"
verses.4:8: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.4:9: "The hands of Zerubbabel founded this house, and his hands will complete it; and you will know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you.
verses.4:10: For who has despised the small days? And they will rejoice and see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven are the eyes of the Lord, which range throughout the whole earth."
verses.4:11: And I answered and said to him, "What are these two olive trees at the right of the lampstand and at its left?"
verses.4:12: And I answered a second time and said to him, "What are the two olive sprigs that are beside the two golden spouts in which are pouring pipes of gold?"
verses.4:13: And he said to me, saying, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
verses.4:14: And he said, "These are the two sons of oil who stand beside the Ruler of the whole earth."
verses.5:1: And I turned and lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a flying scroll.
verses.5:2: And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a flying scroll; its length is twenty cubits, and its width is ten cubits."
verses.5:3: And he said to me, "This is the curse that goes out over the face of all the earth; for every thief, as is written there, will be judged, and everyone who swears will likewise be judged by this.
verses.5:4: 'I will bring it out,' says the Lord of hosts, 'and it will come to the house of the thief, and to the house of the one who swears falsely in My name; and it will remain in the middle of his house, and will consume it, both its timbers and its stones.'"
verses.5:5: And the angel who was speaking in me came out and said to me, "Lift up your eyes, and see what this is that is coming out."
verses.5:6: And I said, "What is it?" And he said, "This is an amphora coming out." And he said, "This is their eye in the whole earth."
verses.5:7: And look, a talent of lead was being carried, and look, one woman sitting in the middle of the amphora.
verses.5:8: And he said, "This is impiety." And he threw her into the middle of the amphora, and put the mass of lead upon its mouth.
verses.5:9: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, two women coming out, and wind was in their wings, and they had wings like the wings of a kite; and they lifted up the amphora between the earth and heaven.
verses.5:10: And I said to the angel who was speaking in me, "Where are these women carrying the amphora?"
verses.5:11: And he said to me, "So that a house may be built for it in the land of Shinar, and that it may be established and placed there upon its base."
verses.6:1: And I turned and lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, four chariots coming out from between two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
verses.6:2: In the first chariot were red horses, and in the second chariot black horses,
verses.6:3: and in the third chariot white horses, and in the fourth chariot dappled and strong horses.
verses.6:4: And I answered and said to the angel who was speaking in me, "What are these, my lord?"
verses.6:5: And the angel answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of heaven, which go out to stand before the Ruler of all the earth."
verses.6:6: The chariot in which the black horses were went out into the land of the north, and the white ones went out after them, and the dappled ones went out to the land of the south.
verses.6:7: And those that were strongest went out and were seeking to go and range through all the earth. And He said, "Go, walk through the earth." And they walked through the earth.
verses.6:8: And He called to me and spoke to me, saying, "Look, those who go out into the land of the north have caused My Spirit to rest in the land of the north."
verses.6:9: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.6:10: "Take from the exile, from Heldai, and from Tobijah, and from Jedaiah; and you will come on that day, and enter the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah, who came from Babylon.
verses.6:11: And you will take gold and silver, and make crowns, and place them on the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest;
verses.6:12: and you will speak to him, saying, 'This is what the Lord of hosts declares, saying: Look, a man, Rising is His name, and beneath Him He will rise, and He will build the temple for the Lord.
verses.6:13: And He Himself will construct the temple for the Lord; and He Himself will bear glory, and He will sit and rule upon His throne; and He will be a priest upon His throne, and a counsel of peace will be between those two.'
verses.6:14: And the crowns will be for Helem, and Tobijah, and Jedaiah, and Hem the son of Zephaniah, as a memorial in the temple of the Lord.
verses.6:15: And those who are far off will come and build in the temple of the Lord; and you will know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you. And this will happen if you earnestly listen to the voice of the Lord your God."
verses.7:1: And it happened in the fourth year of King Darius that the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Chislev.
verses.7:2: And Sharezer and Regem-melech, and the men who were with him, sent to the house of God to implore the face of the Lord,
verses.7:3: so that they might speak to the priests of the house of the Lord of hosts and to the prophets, saying, "Must I weep in the fifth month, or should I sanctify myself, as I have already done for many years?"
verses.7:4: And the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying,
verses.7:5: "Speak to all the people of the land and to the priests, saying, 'When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months through these seventy years, did you really fast a fast for Me?
verses.7:6: And when you ate and drank, did you not eat for yourselves and drink for your own selves?
verses.7:7: Are these not the words that the Lord spoke by the hand of the former prophets, while Jerusalem was still inhabited so that she was wealthy, she herself and the cities around her, and while the south and the plains were inhabited?'"
verses.7:8: And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying,
verses.7:9: "This is what the Lord of hosts declares, saying, 'Render true judgment, and practice mercy and compassions, each one with his brother.
verses.7:10: And do not oppress the widow, the orphan, the foreigner, or the poor person; and let no man devise evil against his brother in his heart.'"
verses.7:11: And they refused to pay attention, and turned away a withdrawing shoulder, and made their ears heavy so that they would not hear.
verses.7:12: And they made their heart like adamant so that they would not hear the law and the words that the Lord of hosts sent in His Spirit through the hand of the former prophets; and great indignation came from the Lord of hosts.
verses.7:13: And it happened that just as He spoke and they did not hear, "so they will cry out and I will not listen," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.7:14: "And I scattered them through all the kingdoms that they do not know, and the land was left desolate by them, because there was no one passing through and returning; and they turned the desirable land into a desert."
verses.8:1: And there came the word of the Lord of hosts, saying:
verses.8:2: "This is what the Lord of hosts says: 'I have been zealous for Zion with great zeal, and with great indignation I have been zealous for her.'"
verses.8:3: This is what the Lord of hosts says: "I have returned to Zion, and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and Jerusalem will be called the city of truth, and the mountain of the Lord of hosts, the sanctified mountain."
verses.8:4: This is what the Lord of hosts says: "Old men and old women will yet dwell in the squares of Jerusalem, and a man's staff will be in his hand because of the multitude of days.
verses.8:5: And the squares of the city will be filled with young boys and girls, playing in its squares."
verses.8:6: This is what the Lord of hosts says: "If it seems difficult in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, will it really be difficult in My eyes?" says the Lord of hosts.
verses.8:7: This is what the Lord of hosts says: "Look, I will save My people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting of the sun.
verses.8:8: And I will bring them, and they will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and they will be a people to Me, and I will be God to them, in truth and in righteousness."
verses.8:9: This is what the Lord of hosts says: "Let your hands be strengthened, you who hear in these days these words through the mouth of the prophets, on the day on which the house of the Lord of hosts was founded, so that the temple might be built.
verses.8:10: For indeed, before those days there was no wage for men, nor was there a wage for livestock; neither for the one going in nor for the one going out was there peace because of tribulation; and I let loose all men, each one against his neighbor.
verses.8:11: But now I will not act toward the remnant of this people according to the former days," says the Lord of hosts,
verses.8:12: "but there will be a seed of peace: the vine will give its fruit, and the earth will give its produce, and the heavens will give their dew; and I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things.
verses.8:13: And it will be that just as you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strengthened."
verses.8:14: For this is what the Lord of hosts says: "Just as I planned to afflict you when your fathers provoked Me to anger," says the Lord,
verses.8:15: "and I did not show mercy, so I have turned and planned in these days to do good to the house of Judah and to Jerusalem. Do not be afraid.
verses.8:16: These therefore are the things that you will do: speak the truth, each one with his neighbor; render truth and the judgment of peace in your gates.
verses.8:17: And do not devise evil in your hearts, each one against his friend, and do not love a lying oath; for all these are things that I hate," says the Lord.
verses.8:18: And the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying,
verses.8:19: "This is what the Lord of hosts says: 'The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth will become joy and gladness and splendid festivals for the house of Judah. Only love truth and peace.'"
verses.8:20: This is what the Lord of hosts says: "Until peoples come and dwell in many cities,
verses.8:21: and the inhabitants go, one to another, saying, 'Let us go and implore the face of the Lord, and seek the Lord of hosts; I also will go.'
verses.8:22: And many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the Lord of hosts in Jerusalem, and to implore the face of the Lord."
verses.8:23: This is what the Lord of hosts says: "In those days, ten men from all the languages of the nations will take hold, and they will take hold of the hem of a Jewish man, saying, 'We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.'"
verses.9:1: The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach and of Damascus, its rest; for the eye of man and of all the tribes of Israel belongs to the Lord.
verses.9:2: Hamath also is within its borders, and Tyre and Sidon; for indeed they have greatly taken wisdom to themselves.
verses.9:3: And Tyre built her stronghold, and heaped up silver like soil, and gold like the mud of the streets.
verses.9:4: Look, the Lord will possess her, and He will strike her strength in the sea, and she herself will be devoured by fire.
verses.9:5: Ashkelon will see and be afraid, and Gaza, and she will grieve exceedingly, and Ekron, because her hope has been confounded; and the king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will not be inhabited.
verses.9:6: And a separator will sit in Ashdod, and I will destroy the pride of the Philistines.
verses.9:7: And I will take away his blood from his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth; and he also will be left for our God, and he will be like a leader in Judah, and Ekron like a Jebusite.
verses.9:8: And I will surround My house with those who serve as soldiers for Me, going and returning; and an oppressor will no longer pass over them, for now I have seen with My eyes.
verses.9:9: Exult greatly, daughter of Zion; shout for joy, daughter of Jerusalem: look, your king will come to you, righteous and a savior; He Himself is poor, and riding on a female donkey and on a colt, the foal of a female donkey.
verses.9:10: And I will destroy the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the bow of war will be shattered; and He will speak peace to the nations, and His authority will be from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the earth.
verses.9:11: You also, by the blood of Your covenant, have released Your prisoners from the pit in which there is no water.
verses.9:12: Turn back to the stronghold, prisoners of hope; today also I announce that I will repay double to you.
verses.9:13: For I have bent Judah for Myself like a bow; I have filled Ephraim; and I will rouse up your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and I will make you like the sword of mighty men.
verses.9:14: And the Lord God will be seen over them, and His javelin will go out like lightning; and the Lord God will sound the trumpet, and will go in the whirlwind of the south.
verses.9:15: The Lord of hosts will protect them; and they will devour, and subdue with the stones of the sling; and drinking, they will become drunk as if from wine, and they will be filled like bowls, and like the horns of the altar.
verses.9:16: And the Lord their God will save them on that day, as the flock of His people, for holy stones will be lifted up over His land.
verses.9:17: For what is His goodness, and what is His beauty, except the grain of the elect, and wine bringing forth virgins?
verses.10:1: Ask the Lord for rain in the late season, and the Lord will make snow, and He will give them a downpour of rain, for each one vegetation in the field.
verses.10:2: For the idols have spoken what is useless, and the diviners have seen falsehood, and the dreamers have spoken in vain; they offered empty comfort. Therefore they have been led away like a flock; they will be afflicted, because they have no shepherd.
verses.10:3: "Against the shepherds My fury is enraged, and I will punish the male goats; for the Lord of hosts has visited His flock, the house of Judah, and has made them like the horse of His glory in war.
verses.10:4: From him the cornerstone, from him the peg, from him the bow of battle, from him every exactor will go out together.
verses.10:5: And they will be like mighty men trampling the mud of the roads in battle; and they will fight, because the Lord is with them, and the riders of horses will be confounded.
verses.10:6: And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them back, because I will have mercy on them; and they will be as they were when I had not cast them off, for I am the Lord their God, and I will hear them.
verses.10:7: And Ephraim will be like mighty men, and their heart will rejoice as from wine; and their children will see and rejoice, and their heart will exult in the Lord.
verses.10:8: I will whistle for them and gather them, because I have redeemed them; and I will multiply them just as they had been multiplied before.
verses.10:9: And I will sow them among the peoples, and from far away they will remember Me; and they will live with their children and return.
verses.10:10: And I will lead them back from the land of Egypt, and from the Assyrians I will gather them, and to the land of Gilead and of Lebanon I will lead them, and no room will be found for them.
verses.10:11: And He will pass through the strait of the sea, and He will strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the river will be confounded; and the pride of Assyria will be humbled, and the scepter of Egypt will depart.
verses.10:12: I will strengthen them in the Lord, and they will walk in His name," says the Lord.
verses.11:1: Open your gates, Lebanon, and let fire consume your cedars.
verses.11:2: Wail, fir tree, because the cedar has fallen, for the magnificent ones have been devastated; wail, oaks of Bashan, for the fortified forest has been cut down.
verses.11:3: The sound of the wailing of the shepherds, because their magnificence has been devastated; the sound of the roaring of lions, for the pride of the Jordan has been devastated.
verses.11:4: This is what the Lord my God says: "Shepherd the sheep of slaughter,
verses.11:5: which those who had possessed them killed and did not grieve, and they sold them, saying, 'Blessed be the Lord! We have become rich,' and their shepherds did not spare them.
verses.11:6: And I will no longer spare the inhabitants of the land," says the Lord. "Look, I will hand men over, each one into the hand of his neighbor and into the hand of his king; and they will crush the land, and I will not rescue them from their hand."
verses.11:7: And I will shepherd the sheep of slaughter because of this, poor of the flock! And I took for myself two staffs: one I called Beauty, and the other I called Cord, and I shepherded the flock.
verses.11:8: And I cut off three shepherds in one month, and my soul grew impatient with them, since indeed their soul also wavered against me.
verses.11:9: And I said, "I will not shepherd you. What is dying, let it die, and what is being cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest each devour the flesh of his neighbor."
verses.11:10: And I took my staff that was called Beauty and severed it, so that I might make void my covenant which I struck with all the peoples.
verses.11:11: And it was made void on that day; and in this way the poor of the flock, who keep watch for me, knew that it is the word of the Lord.
verses.11:12: And I said to them, "If it is good in your eyes, bring my wages; and if not, refrain." And they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver.
verses.11:13: And the Lord said to me, "Throw it to the sculptor, a splendid price at which I was appraised by them." And I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the Lord, to the sculptor.
verses.11:14: And I cut through my second staff, which was named Cord, so that I might dissolve the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
verses.11:15: And the Lord said to me, "Take for yourself once more the equipment of a foolish shepherd.
verses.11:16: For look, I will raise up a shepherd in the land who will not visit the abandoned, will not seek the scattered, and will not heal the broken, and will not nourish what stands; and he will eat the flesh of the fat ones and break apart their hooves.
verses.11:17: Shepherd and idol abandoning the flock: a sword upon his arm and upon his right eye! His arm will be dried up with dryness, and his right eye, growing dark, will be obscured."
verses.12:1: The burden of the word of the Lord upon Israel. The Lord, who stretches out heaven and lays the foundation of the earth and forms the spirit of man within him, says:
verses.12:2: "Look, I will make Jerusalem a lintel of drunkenness for all the surrounding peoples; and Judah also will be in the siege against Jerusalem.
verses.12:3: And it will be on that day: I will make Jerusalem a stone of burden for all the peoples; all who lift it will be torn with gashes, and all the kingdoms of the earth will be gathered against it.
verses.12:4: On that day," says the Lord, "I will strike every horse with stupor and its rider with madness; and over the house of Judah I will open My eyes, and I will strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.
verses.12:5: And the leaders of Judah will say in their heart, 'May the inhabitants of Jerusalem be strengthened for me in the Lord of hosts, their God!'
verses.12:6: On that day I will make the leaders of Judah like a furnace of fire among wood and like a torch of fire in hay; and they will devour to the right and to the left all the surrounding peoples, and Jerusalem will be inhabited again in its own place, in Jerusalem.
verses.12:7: And the Lord will save the tents of Judah as in the beginning, so that the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not boast grandly against Judah.
verses.12:8: On that day the Lord will protect the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and the one among them who stumbles on that day will be like David, and the house of David like that of God, like the angel of the Lord in their sight.
verses.12:9: And it will be on that day: I will seek to crush all the nations that come against Jerusalem.
verses.12:10: And I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and of prayers; and they will look to Me, whom they have pierced, and they will mourn for Him with mourning as over an only-begotten son, and they will grieve over Him as one customarily grieves at the death of a firstborn.
verses.12:11: On that day there will be great mourning in Jerusalem, like the mourning of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
verses.12:12: And the land will mourn, families by families separately: the families of the house of David separately, and their wives separately;
verses.12:13: the families of the house of Nathan separately, and their wives separately; the families of the house of Levi separately, and their wives separately; the families of Shimei separately, and their wives separately;
verses.12:14: all the remaining families, families by families separately, and their wives separately."
verses.13:1: In that day there will be an open fountain for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for the washing of the sinner and of the menstruating woman.
verses.13:2: "And it will happen in that day," says the Lord of hosts, "that I will destroy the names of the idols from the land, and they will not be remembered any longer; and I will remove the false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land."
verses.13:3: And it will happen that when anyone prophesies any longer, his father and his mother, who gave birth to him, will say to him, "You will not live, because you have spoken a lie in the name of the Lord." And his father and his mother, his parents, will pierce him through when he prophesies.
verses.13:4: And it will happen in that day that the prophets will be ashamed, each one because of his vision when he prophesies, nor will they cover themselves with a cloak of sackcloth in order to lie.
verses.13:5: But he will say, "I am not a prophet; I am a man who tills the land, because Adam has been my example from my youth."
verses.13:6: And it will be said to him, "What are these wounds in the middle of your hands?" And he will say, "With these I was wounded in the house of those who loved me."
verses.13:7: "Sword, rouse yourself against My shepherd, and against the man closely joined to Me," says the Lord of hosts. "Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered; and I will turn My hand toward the little ones."
verses.13:8: "And it will happen in all the land," says the Lord, "that two parts in it will be scattered and will perish, and the third part will be left in it.
verses.13:9: And I will lead the third part through the fire, and I will burn them as silver is burned, and I will test them as gold is tested. They will call on My name, and I will hear them. I will say, 'You are My people,' and they will say, 'The Lord is my God.'"
verses.14:1: Look, the days of the Lord will come, and your spoils will be divided in your midst.
verses.14:2: And I will gather all the nations to Jerusalem for battle; and the city will be captured, and the houses will be ravaged, and the women will be violated; and half of the city will go out into captivity, and the rest of the people will not be removed from the city.
verses.14:3: And the Lord will go out and fight against those nations, as He fought on the day of combat.
verses.14:4: And His feet will stand in that day on the Mount of Olives, which is opposite Jerusalem toward the east; and the Mount of Olives will be split from its middle toward the east and toward the west, with a very great chasm; and half of the mountain will be separated toward the north, and half of it toward the south.
verses.14:5: And you will flee to the valley of their mountains, because the valley of the mountains will be joined as far as the nearest place; and you will flee just as you fled from the face of the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah; and the Lord my God will come, and all the holy ones with Him.
verses.14:6: And it will happen in that day: there will not be light, but cold and frost.
verses.14:7: And there will be one day that is known to the Lord, neither day nor night; and at evening time there will be light.
verses.14:8: And it will happen in that day: living waters will go out from Jerusalem, half of them to the eastern sea and half of them to the farthest sea; in summer and in winter they will be there.
verses.14:9: And the Lord will be king over all the earth; in that day the Lord will be one, and His name will be one.
verses.14:10: And all the land will return as far as the desert, from the hill of Rimmon to the south of Jerusalem; and it will be lifted up and will dwell in its place, from the Gate of Benjamin as far as the place of the former gate, and as far as the Gate of the Corners, and from the Tower of Hananel as far as the king's winepresses.
verses.14:11: And they will dwell in it, and there will no longer be a curse, but Jerusalem will sit secure.
verses.14:12: And this will be the plague with which the Lord will strike all the nations that have fought against Jerusalem: the flesh of each one standing on his feet will rot away, and his eyes will rot away in their sockets, and their tongue will rot away in their mouth.
verses.14:13: In that day there will be a great tumult of the Lord among them; and a man will seize the hand of his neighbor, and his hand will be locked against the hand of his neighbor.
verses.14:14: But Judah also will fight against Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the nations all around will be gathered, gold and silver and very many garments.
verses.14:15: And so will be the ruin of the horse, and of the mule, and of the camel, and of the donkey, and of all the beasts of burden that are in those camps, just like this ruin.
verses.14:16: And all who remain from all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to celebrate the Festival of Tabernacles.
verses.14:17: And it will happen: whoever of the families of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, on them there will be no rain.
verses.14:18: And if the family of Egypt does not go up and does not come, neither will it be on them; but there will be the ruin with which the Lord will strike all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tabernacles.
verses.14:19: This will be the sin of Egypt, and this the sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tabernacles.
verses.14:20: In that day, what is on the bridle of the horse will be holy to the Lord; and the pots in the house of the Lord will be like the bowls before the altar.
verses.14:21: And every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be sanctified to the Lord of hosts; and all who sacrifice will come and take from them and cook in them; and there will not be a merchant any longer in the house of the Lord of hosts in that day.

notes.1:4: Latin reads "your most wicked thoughts" (cogitationibus vestris pessimis), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "your evil deeds."
notes.1:8: Latin in profundo ("in the depth") renders a Hebrew term denoting a low hollow or ravine, and varii ("dappled") follows the Septuagint where the Hebrew has "sorrel."
notes.1:9: Latin qui loquebatur in me ("who was speaking in me") literally renders the Hebrew preposition, suggesting interior prophetic communication (also in 1:13, 1:14, 2:2, and 2:7).
notes.1:12: Latin iste jam septuagesimus annus est ("This is now the seventieth year") uses a singular ordinal where the Hebrew has "these seventy years."
notes.1:15: Latin gentes opulentas ("the wealthy nations") reflects a distinctive Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew describes nations "at ease."
notes.2:1: Vulgate chapter numbering places the vision of the four horns and four craftsmen at 2:1-4 (Hebrew 1:18-21) and the measuring-line vision at 2:5-17 (Hebrew 2:1-13).
notes.2:4: Latin per singulos viros ("man by man") is a literal Vulgate rendering of a Hebrew idiom usually taken as "so that no man lifted his head."
notes.2:12: The phrase Post gloriam ("After glory") is debated, understood either as "after restoring glory" or "afterward, in glory." Latin pupillam oculi mei ("the pupil of My eye") reads first-person "My eye," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has third-person "his eye."
notes.2:16: Latin in terra sanctificata ("in the sanctified land") uses the passive participle "sanctified," distinct from the simple adjective "holy" (sancto) in 2:17.
notes.3:1: The Vulgate renders the high priest Joshua's name as Jesus (the Greek and Latin form of Hebrew Yehoshua), a verbal correspondence frequently noted in Christian typological interpretation.
notes.3:4: Latin mutatoriis ("fresh garments," literally "changes of clothing") denotes clean ceremonial or festive robes kept for changing into.
notes.3:5: Latin reads third-person Et dixit ("And he said"), continuing the angel's command, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has first-person "And I said."
notes.3:7: Latin ambulantes ("those who walk") takes the Hebrew term as a plural participle referring to angelic attendants or companions, whereas many Hebrew-based translations read "right of access."
notes.3:8: Latin Orientem ("the Dawn" or "the Rising") follows the Septuagint Anatole as a messianic title for Hebrew Tsemach ("the Branch"); viri portendentes ("foreshadowing men") literally means men who serve as a prophetic portent.
notes.4:1: Latin "in me" literally translates the Hebrew preposition denoting interior prophetic speech, often rendered "with me" in modern versions.
notes.4:2: The Vulgate distinguishes the main top "lamp" ("lampas", for Hebrew "bowl") from the seven "oil lamps" ("lucernae") and reads "seven funnels" ("septem infusoria") where the Hebrew text doubles the number ("seven and seven pipes").
notes.4:7: The Vulgate uniquely renders the Hebrew phrase for shouts of "Grace, grace to it!" as "he will make grace equal to its grace" ("exaequabit gratiam gratiae ejus"), deriving the Hebrew noun from a root meaning to level or equalize.
notes.4:10: The Vulgate has the plural "small days" ("dies parvos", vs. Hebrew "day of small things") and renders the plumb line literally as "the tin stone" ("lapidem stanneum"), referring to a weighted tin plumb bob.
notes.4:12: Latin "spicae" literally means "ears" or "spikes" (here fruiting olive sprigs), and "in which are pouring pipes of gold" ("in quibus sunt suffusoria ex auro") is a Vulgate-distinct rendering where the Hebrew text refers to pipes that empty out golden oil.
notes.5:3: The Vulgate reads "as is written there, will be judged" and "will likewise be judged by this" ("judicabitur"), rendering the Hebrew verb for being purged or cut off in terms of judicial condemnation.
notes.5:6: The Vulgate translates Hebrew "ephah" (a dry grain measure) as "amphora" (a standard Roman storage jar and measure) throughout verses 6-10, and preserves Hebrew "their eye" ("oculus eorum"), where the Septuagint reads "their iniquity".
notes.5:7: The Vulgate renders Hebrew "a round weight/cover of lead was lifted" as "a talent of lead was being carried" ("talentum plumbi portabatur").
notes.5:9: The Vulgate reads "kite" ("milvi") where the Hebrew text has "stork".
notes.6:5: The Vulgate translates Hebrew "ruchot" specifically as "winds" ("venti", rather than "spirits") and reads "to stand" ("ut stent") where the Hebrew says "after presenting themselves".
notes.6:11: The Vulgate reverses the Hebrew order to "gold and silver" ("aurum et argentum") and uses the Latin/Greek name form "Jesus" ("Jesu") for the high priest Joshua.
notes.6:12: The Vulgate renders Hebrew "Branch" ("Tsemach") and its cognate verb as "Rising" ("Oriens") and "will rise" ("orietur"), following the Septuagint "Anatole" (cf. Luke 1:78).
notes.6:13: Latin "et erit sacerdos super solio suo" may be read either as "He will be a priest upon His throne" (uniting royal and priestly offices in the Messiah) or "a priest will be upon his throne" (pointing to the two figures in "between those two").
notes.6:14: The Vulgate reads the name "Hem" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Hen" (meaning "favor" or "grace").
notes.7:2: The Vulgate translates Hebrew Bethel as a common noun phrase, "to the house of God" (ad domum Dei), and places viri ("the men") in the nominative, making Sharezer, Regem-melech, and his companions the subjects who sent to the temple rather than envoys sent from Bethel.
notes.7:3: Where the Hebrew verb denotes abstaining or separating oneself as in a fast, the Vulgate renders sanctificare me ("sanctify myself"), emphasizing ritual consecration.
notes.7:13: The Vulgate reads locutus est ("He spoke") rather than the Hebrew "He called," and renders the second clause in the future tense (clamabunt et non exaudiam, "they will cry out and I will not listen") rather than a past habitual action.
notes.8:3: The Vulgate includes exercituum ("of hosts") in the opening formula (where the Hebrew has only "the LORD") and renders the final title as mons sanctificatus ("the sanctified mountain") rather than "the mountain of holiness."
notes.8:10: The Vulgate reverses the Hebrew order of "going out and coming in" to introeunti ... exeunti ("going in ... going out") and translates Hebrew "from the foe" abstractly as prae tribulatione ("because of tribulation").
notes.8:20: The Vulgate reads usquequo veniant populi et habitent in civitatibus multis ("Until peoples come and dwell in many cities"), translating the Hebrew phrase as a temporal clause with a finite verb ("and dwell") rather than "It will yet be that peoples will come, even the inhabitants of many cities."
notes.9:6: The Vulgate translates the rare Hebrew term mamzer ("mixed people" or "illegitimate one") as separator ("a separator"), reflecting an etymological interpretation of the word as one who separates or estranges.
notes.9:8: Rather than camping "because of an army, because of those passing back and forth," the Vulgate renders circumdabo domum meam ex his qui militant mihi euntes et revertentes ("I will surround My house with those who serve as soldiers for Me, going and returning"), portraying protective forces patrolling God's house.
notes.9:9: The Vulgate reads salvator ("a savior," active, matching the Septuagint) rather than the passive Hebrew "saved/victorious," translates "afflicted/humble" as pauper ("poor"), and makes both donkeys feminine (asinam ... asinae), aligning with Matthew 21:5.
notes.9:11: Whereas the Hebrew shifts to the first person ("I have set your prisoners free"), the Vulgate uses the second-person verb emisisti ("You have released"), which traditional Latin exegesis often reads as addressed to the Messianic King of verses 9-10 releasing captives by the blood of His covenant (testamenti).
notes.9:17: The Vulgate frames the verse as a single rhetorical question with nisi ("except") and renders Hebrew "grain [for] young men" as frumentum electorum ("the grain of the elect") alongside vinum germinans virgines ("wine bringing forth virgins").
notes.10:1: The Vulgate reads nives ("snow" or "snows"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to storm clouds or lightning and the Septuagint reads "visions."
notes.10:7: Latin Et erunt quasi fortes Ephraim takes indeclinable Ephraim as a collective plural subject ("And Ephraim will be like mighty men"), though it can also be read as genitive ("And they will be like the mighty men of Ephraim").
notes.10:11: The Vulgate renders Hebrew distress/straits concretely as in maris freto ("through the strait of the sea"), and reads confundentur ("will be confounded") where the Hebrew has "will dry up."
notes.11:5: The Vulgate reads qui possederant ("those who had possessed them") and non dolebant ("did not grieve"), where the Hebrew has "their buyers" and "are not held guilty."
notes.11:7: The Vulgate preserves the future tense pascam ("I will shepherd") before shifting to the past, treats o pauperes gregis as a vocative ("O poor of the flock"), and renders the second staff's name as Funiculum ("Cord") rather than Hebrew "Union."
notes.11:8: Latin contracta est anima mea literally means "my soul was contracted" (an idiom for growing impatient), and variavit ("wavered" or "changed") is a Vulgate-distinct rendering where the Hebrew means "loathed."
notes.11:13: The Vulgate translates Hebrew yotzer ("potter") as statuarium ("sculptor" or "molder of statues"), repeated twice in this verse.
notes.11:17: The Vulgate renders Hebrew "worthless shepherd" as two vocative nouns, O pastor, et idolum ("Shepherd and idol").
notes.12:2: The Vulgate renders Hebrew sap (which can mean either "bowl/cup" or "threshold/lintel") as superliminare ("lintel"), giving superliminare crapulae ("a lintel of drunkenness").
notes.12:5: The Vulgate reads a passive jussive verb, Confortentur ("May ... be strengthened"), where the Hebrew has a noun ("are a strength to me").
notes.12:8: The Vulgate uses the genitive quasi Dei ("like that of God," referring back to "the house"), whereas the Hebrew reads "like God."
notes.12:10: The Vulgate reads ut doleri solet in morte primogeniti ("as one customarily grieves at the death of a firstborn"), making "at the death of" explicit where the Hebrew reads "like bitter weeping over a firstborn."
notes.13:1: Vulgate reads "peccatoris et menstruatae" ("of the sinner and of the menstruating woman"), using concrete personal nouns where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the abstract nouns "sin and impurity."
notes.13:5: A notable Vulgate-distinct reading: "quoniam Adam exemplum meum" ("because Adam has been my example"), taking Hebrew "adam" as the first man Adam tilling the ground, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "for a man acquired me" (or "sold me").
notes.13:6: Vulgate "in medio manuum tuarum" ("in the middle of your hands") translates literally the Hebrew idiom "between your hands" (often understood in Hebrew as the chest or back).
notes.13:9: Vulgate reads second-person "Populus meus es" ("You are My people") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has third-person "It is My people." The Latin collective singular pronouns ("Ipse... eum... ipse") referring to the remnant are rendered "they/them" for clarity in English.
notes.14:1: Vulgate reads the plural "venient dies Domini" ("the days of the Lord will come"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the singular "a day is coming for the Lord."
notes.14:5: Vulgate has three distinct readings here: "montium eorum" ("their mountains," vs. Hebrew "My mountains"), "usque ad proximum" ("as far as the nearest place," rendering Hebrew "Azal" as a common noun rather than a place name), and "cum eo" ("with Him," agreeing with the Septuagint against Hebrew "with you").
notes.14:6: Vulgate "non erit lux, sed frigus et gelu" ("there will not be light, but cold and frost") follows the Septuagint in resolving a difficult Hebrew phrase often translated "the bright ones will congeal" or "dwindle."
notes.14:10: Vulgate "revertetur... usque ad desertum, de colle Remmon" ("will return as far as the desert, from the hill of Rimmon") renders Hebrew "Geba" as a common noun ("hill") and "Arabah" as "desert," contrasting with the Hebrew Masoretic Text "will be turned into a plain from Geba to Rimmon." Vulgate also has plural "portam angulorum" ("Gate of the Corners").
notes.14:14: Vulgate "adversus Jerusalem" ("against Jerusalem") interprets the Hebrew preposition in a hostile sense rather than locatively ("at/in Jerusalem").
